titleZh: 真正吸引人接觸的亮點

brief.meaningEn: The main feature that catches interest and makes someone want to engage further.
brief.meaningZh: 主要抓住興趣，令人想繼續接觸的特點。
brief.grammar: the real hook of a story is + feature; identify what initially draws the person in.
brief.register: Conventional hook metaphor for attraction. Real emphasises the feature judged most compelling, not that other attractions are fake.
brief.boundaryZh: 吸引起步不保證持續喜歡、內容完整或客觀最好；需說明對誰有何吸引。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可區分最先吸引的元素與最後重視的內容，不把它們強行當同一事。
brief.outcomeZh: 能具體說出吸引人開始的特點，保留之後評價。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The real hook of the novel is its unusual narrator.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 19, table 2, row 3; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: For me, the real hook of the podcast was hearing one event described by three neighbours; it made me want to listen beyond the trailer and compare their accounts.
listening.zh: 對我而言，節目真正吸引人的是三位鄰居講同一事件，讓我想不只聽預告，繼續比較敘述。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼是吸引說話者繼續聽的主要特點？

options.en: Different accounts of one event from three neighbours.
options.zh: 三位鄰居對同一事件的不同敘述。

options.en: A confirmed solution announced before any account was heard.
options.zh: 未聽任何敘述前已宣布的確定答案。

options.en: The fact that the trailer contained the entire series.
options.zh: 預告已包含全系列的事實。

options.en: The familiar title rather than the neighbours’ perspectives.
options.zh: 熟悉標題，而非鄰居視角。

listening.explanationZh: 三種敘述引起比較興趣，未說先有答案或全聽完。

reply.promptZh: 甚麼吸引你不只聽預告，而想繼續？
reply.promptEn: What made you want to listen beyond the trailer?

options.en: I wanted to compare three neighbours’ versions of the same event.
options.zh: 我想比較三位鄰居對同一事件的版本。

options.en: The real hook was the chance to hear one event from three perspectives.
options.zh: 真正吸引處是能從三種視角聽同一事件。

options.en: The differing accounts made me curious about how their experiences connected.
options.zh: 不同敘述令我好奇他們經歷怎樣相連。

options.en: Hearing several viewpoints on one event gave me a reason to keep listening.
options.zh: 一件事有幾種觀點，給我繼續聽的理由。

reply.explanationZh: 四句給具體吸引來源，不只重複好聽。

scene.promptZh: 一本故事開頭由不可靠的時鐘講時間，你因這奇特敘事角度想再讀，但還未讀完整本。哪句準確？

options.en: For me, the real hook is the unusual narrator.
options.zh: 對我而言，真正吸引處是奇特敘事者。

options.en: I have already judged the ending after completing the whole book.
options.zh: 我已讀完整本，判斷結尾。

options.en: The narrator’s identity made me put the book aside without interest.
options.zh: 敘事者身分讓我毫無興趣地放下書。

scene.explanationZh: 奇特角度引起續讀，不是已完或失興趣。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 the real hook 得出？

options.en: A feature is being identified as especially attractive.
options.zh: 某特點被指出特別吸引。

options.en: The whole work has already been judged successful in the long term.
options.zh: 整部作品已被判長期成功。

options.en: We need context to know whom it attracts and why.
options.zh: 需情境才知吸引誰及為甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 起步吸引與長期整體評價不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問「有三種視角，就表示你已信了其中一個版本嗎？」你只是想繼續比較。哪句回應準確？

options.en: It drew my interest, but I have not decided how the accounts fit together.
options.zh: 它引起興趣，但我未決定各敘述怎樣相連。

options.en: Yes, wanting to compare them was my final choice of the most accurate account.
options.zh: 對，想比較已是我最後選了最準確敘述。

options.en: I was interested only in the title and did not want to hear the neighbours.
options.zh: 我只對標題有興趣，不想聽鄰居。

dialogue.explanationZh: 想繼續是吸引效果，不是內容已定或沒興趣。

speaking.en: The real hook was the unusual point of view, but I still wanted to see how the story developed.
speaking.zh: 真正吸引處是奇特視角，但我仍想看故事怎樣發展。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清起步吸引與後續體驗。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替校園種植活動寫邀請，不想只用「好玩」；新同學可親自選一株植物、隔周觀察改變，這正是試看者最想參加的原因。你想把這具體亮點放在邀請開頭，仍說清實際需定期照料。用一至兩句英文建議文案。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用試看者指出的具體選植觀察作亮點，連到邀請排序並保留照料需要，不只空泛讚好或保證長期投入。

examples.en: The real hook is choosing a plant and watching it change over the weeks, so we should lead with that. The invitation must also explain the regular care involved.
examples.zh: 真正吸引處是選一株植物，看它幾周間改變，所以應先寫這點。邀請亦需解釋定期照料。

examples.en: For new members, the real hook is having a plant of their own to observe. Let’s describe that experience clearly alongside the care schedule.
examples.zh: 對新成員，真正吸引處是有自己一株植物觀察。把體驗與照料時間表一起寫清楚吧。

takeaways.en: The real hook of the exhibition was the chance to compare an artist’s first sketch with the finished piece.
takeaways.zh: 展覽真正吸引處，是能把藝術家首稿與成品比較。

takeaways.en: The real hook caught my attention, but the later details gave me a reason to stay.
takeaways.zh: 主要亮點抓住我注意，後來細節則讓我留下。

brief.meaningEn: A power to attract or hold someone’s interest through feeling.
brief.meaningZh: 透過感受吸引或留住某人興趣的力量。
brief.grammar: a story has emotional pull; feel the emotional pull of + person/place/work; explain the feeling or connection involved.
brief.register: Conventional force metaphor for emotional attraction; no literal pulling is involved.
brief.boundaryZh: 情感吸引不表示所有人同感、理性考慮消失或內容必定真實；需指出個人反應。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可被觸動仍有疑問，不把感受強度代替查事實或作決定。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述具體情感吸引，保留其他判斷。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The story has strong emotional pull despite its simple plot.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 19, table 2, row 4; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The story’s emotional pull came from the two friends trying to repair their relationship; I wanted to know whether they could speak honestly, even when I questioned some of their choices.
listening.zh: 故事的情感吸引來自兩朋友嘗試修補關係；我想知他們能否坦白交談，儘管質疑某些選擇。

options.en: Concern about the friends’ relationship held the speaker’s interest.
options.zh: 對朋友關係的關心留住說話者興趣。

options.en: The speaker approved of all the choices without reservation.
options.zh: 說話者毫無保留贊同所有選擇。

options.en: The friends had already settled their conflict before the narrator became interested.
options.zh: 敘述者感興趣前，兩朋友已解決衝突。

options.en: The relationship had no effect on the speaker’s interest.
options.zh: 關係對說話者興趣沒有影響。

listening.explanationZh: 想知能否坦白交談顯示仍關注未定關係；不是衝突早已解決，興趣也不等於認同全部選擇。

reply.promptZh: 故事甚麼地方讓你投入？
reply.promptEn: What drew you into the story emotionally?

options.en: I cared about whether the two friends could rebuild honest communication.
options.zh: 我關心兩朋友能否重建坦白溝通。

options.en: Its emotional pull came from their attempt to repair the relationship.
options.zh: 情感吸引來自他們嘗試修補關係。

options.en: Their difficulty made me want to hear what they would say to each other.
options.zh: 他們的困難讓我想聽彼此會說甚麼。

options.en: I kept following the story because their friendship mattered to me.
options.zh: 我繼續跟故事，因在意他們的友誼。

reply.explanationZh: 四句給關係上的情感連結，不以贊同全部代投入。

scene.promptZh: 一幅畫讓你想起祖父等你放學的溫暖，你願意停留細看，卻還不知道畫家背景。哪句準確？

options.en: The painting has emotional pull for me because it recalls that familiar care.
options.zh: 畫因喚起熟悉關懷，對我有情感牽引。

options.en: I already know the painter intended to depict my grandfather.
options.zh: 我已知畫家有意描我祖父。

options.en: My interest comes from what I already know about the painter’s background.
options.zh: 我的興趣來自已知的畫家背景。

scene.explanationZh: 自己的關懷回憶支持吸引；畫家背景仍未知，亦未給他想描祖父的意圖。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 emotional pull 得出？

options.en: A feeling helps attract or hold someone’s attention.
options.zh: 某感受幫吸引或留住注意。

options.en: The emotional response establishes the factual truth of the account.
options.zh: 情感反應確立敘述事實為真。

options.en: The person’s association may explain the attraction.
options.zh: 當事人的聯想可解釋吸引。

contrast.explanationZh: 感受與事實準確不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友問「你在意角色，就表示認同她那個決定嗎？」你仍對決定有保留。哪句準確？

options.en: I can care about her situation while questioning what she chose to do.
options.zh: 我可在意她處境，同時質疑她所選行動。

options.en: Yes, my interest means I have accepted the decision as the best option.
options.zh: 對，我有興趣表示已接受該決定是最佳。

options.en: I was following only the sequence of events and felt nothing about the friendship.
options.zh: 我只跟事件次序，對友誼沒有感受。

dialogue.explanationZh: 情感牽引與價值判斷可分開。

speaking.en: The scene has emotional pull for me, though I still have questions about the decision it shows.
speaking.zh: 那幕對我有情感牽引，但我仍對其中決定有問題。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再保留投入與疑問。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們想選一段舊校舍故事放在周年刊物，試讀者被一位工友多年記住學生名字的細節打動。你想肯定它的情感吸引，同時請編輯核對人名及年份，避免只靠感動就刊出。用一至兩句英文提出建議。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用已給關懷細節支持情感吸引，提出保留及查證，不把試讀感動當事實已全核實。

examples.en: The detail about remembering students’ names gives the account emotional pull. We should preserve it while checking the names and dates before publication.
examples.zh: 記住學生名字的細節讓敘述有情感牽引。我們應保留它，同時在刊登前核對姓名日期。

examples.en: The story has emotional pull because it shows years of personal care, but that response should lead us to handle the details carefully rather than skip the checks.
examples.zh: 故事呈現多年個人關懷，所以有情感牽引，但這反應應讓我們慎重處理細節，而非省核對。

takeaways.en: The emotional pull of the letters came from their small acts of care.
takeaways.zh: 書信的情感牽引來自其中小小關懷行動。

takeaways.en: I felt the emotional pull of the scene without being certain what I would do in the character’s place.
takeaways.zh: 我感到那幕情感牽引，卻未肯定自己處同一位置會怎樣做。

brief.meaningEn: Attract people’s interest and encourage them to engage with an experience.
brief.meaningZh: 吸引人的興趣，令人願意投入某體驗。
brief.grammar: a strong opening draws people in; drew in past, has drawn in perfect; pronouns go between draw and in.
brief.register: Common attention-attracting phrasal verb. This lesson is involvement, not physically pulling someone into a room.
brief.boundaryZh: 吸引投入不等於留到最後、完全同意或每人都有同一反應；需描述實際接觸。
brief.misconceptionZh: 人數增加可另有原因，不單憑到場數量就保證每人投入。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說出吸引的特點及觀察到的投入，保留結果範圍。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A strong opening draws people in.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 19, table 2, row 5; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The opening question drew us in because it connected the exhibition with an ordinary decision we had all faced, and we began comparing our own responses.
listening.zh: 開場問題把展覽連到大家面對過的日常決定，吸引我們投入，開始比較自己回應。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼顯示觀眾開始投入？

options.en: They connected the question with experience and compared their responses.
options.zh: 他們把問題連到經驗，並比較回應。

options.en: They left before hearing the opening question.
options.zh: 他們未聽開場問題就離開。

options.en: The organiser only counted people entering, without observing any discussion.
options.zh: 主辦者只點入場人數，沒有觀察討論。

options.en: The account reports that they stayed for every remaining activity.
options.zh: 敘述報告他們參與其餘每項活動。

listening.explanationZh: 比較各自回應是實際投入線索，不只是點入場人數，也未說其後留足全程。

reply.promptZh: 開場問題為甚麼讓你們投入？
reply.promptEn: Why did the opening question engage your group?

options.en: It connected the exhibition with a decision familiar to us.
options.zh: 它把展覽連到我們熟悉的決定。

options.en: It drew us in by giving us something personal to compare.
options.zh: 它給我們可親自比較的事，吸引投入。

options.en: We could relate the question to experience and talk about our responses.
options.zh: 我們可把問題連到經驗，談自己回應。

options.en: It gave the group a meaningful starting point for discussion.
options.zh: 它給小組有意義的討論起點。

reply.explanationZh: 四句給已知個人關聯，不預設留到最後。

scene.promptZh: 故事首段讓你看到人物面臨一個熟悉兩難，你放下手機，想讀下去，尚未看結尾。哪句準確？

options.en: The opening drew me in through the character’s dilemma.
options.zh: 開頭透過角色兩難吸引我投入。

options.en: I had already finished the ending before the opening caught my interest.
options.zh: 開頭引起興趣前，我已看完結尾。

options.en: I put the story aside because the dilemma had no connection with me.
options.zh: 我因兩難與自己無關而放下故事。

scene.explanationZh: 熟悉兩難及想續讀支持吸引，不是已完成或不相關。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 drew people in 得出？

options.en: It attracted some engagement in the context.
options.zh: 它在情境中吸引投入。

options.en: Those attracted necessarily stayed through the entire experience.
options.zh: 被吸引的人必定留足整個體驗。

options.en: The account should explain how their interest was noticed.
options.zh: 敘述應說明怎樣觀察到興趣。

contrast.explanationZh: 起步投入與最終留到哪階段不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問「大家開頭有交流，所以後面全參加了？」但你只有開場觀察。哪句準確？

options.en: I can describe the opening engagement, but I have not checked attendance at the later activities.
options.zh: 我可描述開場投入，但未查後來活動參與。

options.en: Yes, their first responses tell us they completed the whole programme.
options.zh: 對，最初回應告訴我們他們完成全程。

options.en: No discussion took place; we only counted people entering the room.
options.zh: 沒有討論；我們只點入房人數。

dialogue.explanationZh: 應保留實際交流，不擴成全程，也不改成只計人數。

speaking.en: The opening drew me in, but I still needed to see how the rest of the story developed.
speaking.zh: 開頭吸引我投入，但仍需看後面故事怎樣發展。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清起步興趣及後續體驗。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為新手陶藝活動設計入門環節，先讓來賓摸一塊可試做的小泥片，再選想問的問題；試玩者因此願意開始。你想保留這個吸引起步的做法，下一次再觀察他們後續需要，尚未知道全課成效。用一至兩句英文說明。
writing.selfCheckZh: 把可試做泥片連到新人願開始，提出保留及觀察後續支援，不將起步參與當整課已成功。

examples.en: The small clay sample drew people in by letting them try something before asking questions. We should keep that opening and observe what support they need next.
examples.zh: 小泥片讓人先試再問，吸引他們投入。我們應保留這開頭，再觀察後續需甚麼支援。

examples.en: Letting newcomers shape a little clay can draw them in without asking for a finished piece straight away. It is a starting point, not a complete measure of the workshop.
examples.zh: 讓新人捏小泥片可吸引投入，不要求立即做成品。這是起點，不是工作坊全部成效指標。

takeaways.en: The familiar problem drew us in before the speaker introduced the more difficult questions.
takeaways.zh: 講者提出較難問題前，熟悉困難先吸引我們投入。

takeaways.en: Her opening scene draws people in by making the character’s choice matter.
takeaways.zh: 她的開場讓角色選擇變得重要，吸引人投入。

titleEn: paint with too broad a brush

brief.meaningEn: Describe a group or situation in terms so general that important differences are lost.
brief.meaningZh: 概括群體或情況時過於籠統，忽略重要差異。
brief.grammar: paint with too broad a brush; painting in progress; too marks excessive breadth, not the claim that all generalisation is wrong.
brief.register: Established painting metaphor for overgeneralising. Unlike tar everyone with the same brush, it does not require assigning a negative quality.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點是概括超出依據，正面負面均可；不表示任何概括都不能用，也不靠一個反例便否定所有共同點。
brief.misconceptionZh: 應調整範圍及保留差異，不是把有依據共通處全刪。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出說法超出哪個樣本或差異，改成有範圍的描述。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.expression: painting with too broad a brush
sources.sentence: Calling all teenagers careless is painting with too broad a brush.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 19, table 2, row 6; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: Saying that every volunteer wanted a public speaking role was painting with too broad a brush: some wanted to speak, while others preferred preparing the materials or welcoming guests.
listening.zh: 說每位義工都想公開發言，是過度概括：有些想說，有些偏備料或接待。

options.en: Different preferences for how to contribute.
options.zh: 以不同方式貢獻的偏好。

options.en: A complete lack of interest in helping with the event.
options.zh: 對幫活動完全沒興趣。

options.en: A rule that no volunteer could speak publicly.
options.zh: 義工全不可公開說話的規則。

options.en: A plan to make the materials team speak first.
options.zh: 讓備料組先發言的計劃。

listening.explanationZh: 角色偏好不同，不是全不願助或全禁發言。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼說每位義工都想公開發言太籠統？
reply.promptEn: Why was saying every volunteer wanted public speaking too general?

options.en: Some preferred preparing materials or welcoming guests.
options.zh: 有些偏好備料或接待。

options.en: It was painting with too broad a brush because their preferred roles differed.
options.zh: 因偏好角色不同，那是在過度概括。

options.en: Wanting to help did not mean everyone wanted the same speaking role.
options.zh: 想幫忙不表示人人想同一發言角色。

options.en: The claim overlooked the other ways volunteers wanted to contribute.
options.zh: 說法忽略義工想作貢獻的其他方式。

reply.explanationZh: 四句給已知差異，不把角色不同改成不願幫助。

scene.promptZh: 你訪問三位學生喜歡實作，摘要卻寫全校學生都不愛閱讀；你沒有全校資料。哪句修正準確？

options.en: That paints with too broad a brush; report what these students said without assigning a view to the whole school.
options.zh: 那過度概括；報這幾位所說，不替全校定看法。

options.en: The three interviews establish the whole school’s view of reading.
options.zh: 三次訪問確立全校對閱讀的看法。

options.en: Their interest in practical work establishes that these three students do not enjoy reading.
options.zh: 喜歡實作確立了這三位學生不喜歡閱讀。

scene.explanationZh: 三人樣本不能代表全校；即使只談三人，喜歡實作也不直接確立不喜歡閱讀。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不像 painting with too broad a brush？

options.en: Giving one preference to a whole group despite known differences.
options.zh: 明知有差異仍給全群體同一偏好。

options.en: Describing what the three interviewed students said and naming that limited sample.
options.zh: 描述三位受訪學生所說，並指明樣本有限。

options.en: Treating a small sample as a complete account of the whole school.
options.zh: 把小樣本當全校完整敘述。

contrast.explanationZh: 有範圍描述保留資料限制，不是過度概括。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說「那就不能總結任何共同點了？」你只想修正全體同偏好的說法。哪句最好？

options.en: We can describe supported similarities while keeping the different role preferences clear.
options.zh: 我們可描述有依據共同點，同時保留不同角色偏好。

options.en: Yes, the different roles mean we cannot mention their shared willingness to help.
options.zh: 對，角色不同表示不能提共同願幫忙。

options.en: The simplest fix is to replace all role preferences with one preferred task.
options.zh: 最簡單改法是把所有角色偏好換成同一任務。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可同時有共通處及差異，不須全刪或再強行統一。

speaking.en: That paints with too broad a brush; we need to keep the differences within the group visible.
speaking.zh: 那過度概括；我們需保留群體內的差異。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再指出概括範圍。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你整理社區交通問卷，部分長者願用手機查班次，部分偏好站牌；草稿卻一概寫長者拒絕科技。你想改成忠於這批回覆，並保留兩種查詢途徑供選。用一至兩句英文給編輯建議。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以這批手機與站牌偏好修正全體拒科技的說法，提出保留選擇，不把年齡當既定能力或超出樣本。

examples.en: Saying older residents reject technology paints with too broad a brush; these replies show different preferences. We should report both the phone and noticeboard options.
examples.zh: 說長者拒絕科技是過度概括；這批回覆顯示不同偏好。我們應報手機及站牌兩種選項。

examples.en: Let’s avoid painting with too broad a brush and describe what the respondents actually chose. Keeping both ways to check the timetable would reflect that variety.
examples.zh: 避免過度概括，描述回應者實際選甚麼吧。保留兩種查班次方法會反映多樣性。

takeaways.en: Calling every delay careless paints with too broad a brush when the causes differ.
takeaways.zh: 原因不同時，把每次延誤都叫粗心，是過度概括。

takeaways.en: We avoided painting with too broad a brush by describing the differences among the replies.
takeaways.zh: 我們描述回覆之間的差異，避免過度概括。

brief.meaningEn: Have a preference for one possibility without necessarily making a final commitment.
brief.meaningZh: 對某個可能選項有偏好，未必已作最後承諾。
brief.grammar: lean towards a choice / lean more towards it; both signal a preference without saying the decision is final. More strengthens the comparison with another option.
brief.register: Common figurative direction pattern; towards is usual British wording, toward is also standard.
brief.boundaryZh: 傾向不是已預約、已買或永不改變，也不必是壓倒性偏好；仍可有待查條件。
brief.misconceptionZh: 說出偏好可有理由，同時保留最後選擇未定。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明有理由的暫時偏好及尚待核對部分。

listening.en: We are leaning towards the morning slot because more volunteers are available then, but we need to confirm the room before making the final booking.
listening.zh: 我們較傾向早上時段，因更多義工有空，但正式預約前需確認房間。
listening.promptZh: 小組的選擇到了哪一步？

options.en: A reasoned preference, with room confirmation still pending.
options.zh: 有理由的偏好，房間確認仍待做。

options.en: A final confirmed room booking for the morning.
options.zh: 早上房間的最終確認預約。

options.en: A rejection of the morning because fewer volunteers are free.
options.zh: 因較少義工有空而拒早上。

options.en: No comparison of volunteer availability had been made.
options.zh: 尚未比較義工空檔。

listening.explanationZh: leaning及but need confirm 分偏好與落實，有義工理由。

reply.promptZh: 你們目前較想選哪個時段，為甚麼？
reply.promptEn: Which slot do you currently prefer, and why?

options.en: The morning, because more volunteers are available, though the room is not confirmed.
options.zh: 早上，因更多義工有空，但房間未確認。

options.en: We are leaning towards the morning because it suits more of the volunteers.
options.zh: 我們較傾向早上，因配合更多義工。

options.en: The morning looks more promising on staffing, with the room still to check.
options.zh: 人手方面早上較可行，房間仍需查。

options.en: Our current preference is the earlier slot based on who can help.
options.zh: 按能幫忙的人手，目前偏好較早時段。

reply.explanationZh: 四句說有理由偏好，不把房間報成已定。

scene.promptZh: 兩本書都可借，你稍想先讀有熟悉題材那本，明天還會翻另一篇樣章才決定。哪句準確？

options.en: I am leaning towards the familiar topic, but I have not decided yet.
options.zh: 我較傾向熟悉題材，但未決定。

options.en: I have already borrowed it and finished comparing both books.
options.zh: 我已借它，也比完兩本。

options.en: I have rejected the familiar topic without looking at the other sample.
options.zh: 我未看另一樣章就拒熟悉題材。

scene.explanationZh: 有偏好但仍待樣章，不是已選或反方向。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 leaning towards A 得出？

options.en: A is currently the preferred possibility.
options.zh: A 目前是較偏好的可能選項。

options.en: The final arrangement has already been confirmed.
options.zh: 最後安排已確認。

options.en: Further information could still change the choice.
options.zh: 更多資訊仍可能改變選擇。

contrast.explanationZh: 傾向不同於落實。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問「既然傾向早上，我現在就公布房間已訂了？」但房間仍未回覆。哪句最好？

options.en: We lean towards the morning, but the room is not confirmed; let us wait before announcing a booking.
options.zh: 我們傾向早上，但房間尚未確認；公布預約前先等場地回覆。

options.en: Yes, use the volunteer preference as the confirmation from the venue.
options.zh: 對，把義工偏好當場地確認。

options.en: Say we have no preference at all until the venue replies.
options.zh: 場地回覆前，說我們毫無偏好。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可有未落實偏好，不當已訂也不否定已知傾向。

speaking.en: I am leaning towards this option, but I still need to check one important detail.
speaking.zh: 我較傾向這選項，但仍需核對一項重要細節。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再保留偏好與待查條件。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替家族故事小冊選封面，較想用祖母手寫標題，因與內容連得上，但要先問她是否同意公開，再決定。你想向設計同伴表達傾向與尚待同意的步驟，不擅自說已獲批。用一至兩句英文寫訊息。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以與故事連結說明偏好，保留先問同意再定稿，不把藝術選擇當已獲公開許可。

examples.en: I am leaning towards using Grandma’s handwritten title because it connects with the family stories. Let’s ask her permission before we make it final.
examples.zh: 我較傾向用祖母手寫標題，因它與家族故事相連。最後定稿前，先問她同意吧。

examples.en: I am leaning towards the handwritten cover, but I still want to check that she is happy for it to be shared publicly.
examples.zh: 我較傾向手寫封面，但仍想確認她樂意公開分享。

takeaways.en: She was leaning towards the shorter route while checking whether the meeting point suited everyone.
takeaways.zh: 她較傾向短路線，同時查集合點是否配合大家。

takeaways.en: After trying both formats, the volunteers leaned more towards short evening sessions.
takeaways.zh: 試過兩種形式後，義工較傾向短時間的晚間活動。

titleZh: 已固定而不能輕易改動

brief.meaningEn: Fixed or settled rather than open to alteration; often negated to allow further changes.
brief.meaningZh: 已固定或定下，不再開放改動；常以否定表示仍可調整。
brief.grammar: the plan is/is not set in stone; set stays the same in past and participle; attend to not before interpreting the status.
brief.register: Established stone-inscription image for fixed arrangements. It describes how settled something is, not a physical inability to change it.
brief.boundaryZh: not set in stone 表示仍可改，不等於已取消、改好或完全沒計劃；何時及由誰改仍需另說。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可調整與可任意自行更改不同，仍要確認影響及通知。
brief.outcomeZh: 能準確說明計劃固定程度，分清可能、提議及已完成改動。

listening.en: The order of the sessions is not set in stone; we can discuss a swap if it helps the visiting group, but no change has been agreed yet.
listening.zh: 環節次序尚未固定；若對到訪小組有幫助可討論調換，但還未議定改動。

options.en: It can still be discussed, with no swap agreed yet.
options.zh: 仍可討論，尚未議定調換。

options.en: A swap has already been approved and announced.
options.zh: 調換已批准宣布。

options.en: The entire visit has been cancelled.
options.zh: 整個到訪已取消。

options.en: The order cannot be discussed under the current plan.
options.zh: 按目前計劃，次序不能討論。

listening.explanationZh: not固定及can discuss容許調整，but no agreed保留未改。

reply.promptZh: 我們能否談談把兩個環節調換？
reply.promptEn: Could we discuss swapping two sessions?

options.en: Yes, the order is still open to discussion, though nothing has changed yet.
options.zh: 可以，次序仍可討論，但尚未改。

options.en: Yes, it is not set in stone; we can consider what helps the visiting group.
options.zh: 可以，尚未固定；可考慮怎樣幫到訪小組。

options.en: A swap can be considered before we agree and notify people.
options.zh: 可先考慮調換，再議定通知。

options.en: The current sequence is a plan we can review rather than a final restriction.
options.zh: 目前次序是可檢視計劃，不是最後限制。

reply.explanationZh: 四句容許討論，不宣稱已批准。

scene.promptZh: 班級草案寫周五分享，老師說仍可按小組空檔討論，但新日期未確認。哪句準確？

options.en: The date is not set in stone, although we have not chosen a replacement.
options.zh: 日期未固定，雖然未選替代日。

options.en: Friday’s session has already been moved to an agreed date.
options.zh: 周五環節已移到議定日期。

options.en: No proposal exists because the date can change.
options.zh: 因日期可改，所以沒有方案。

scene.explanationZh: 有草案也可開放調整，不是已改或沒計劃。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 not set in stone 得出？

options.en: The arrangement may still be altered.
options.zh: 安排仍可能改動。

options.en: A particular replacement has already been approved.
options.zh: 某個替代方案已批准。

options.en: The process for making a change may still matter.
options.zh: 改動程序仍可能重要。

contrast.explanationZh: 可改不決定已批哪個改法。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問「既然沒固定，我可直接通知大家換了？」但仍需與到訪小組協調。哪句最好？

options.en: Discuss the swap and confirm it with the group before sending a changed timetable.
options.zh: 先與小組討論確認調換，再寄改後時間表。

options.en: Yes, the possibility of a change is enough to announce that it has happened.
options.zh: 可以，有可能改就足以宣布已改。

options.en: Announce the swap first and ask the visiting group afterwards whether it helps.
options.zh: 先宣布調換，再問到訪小組是否有幫助。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可以討論的次序仍需先協調確認，不能把可能性當完成，也不應先宣布才問受影響小組。

speaking.en: The plan is not set in stone, but we should agree on any changes before announcing them.
speaking.zh: 計劃未固定，但宣布前應議定任何改動。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清彈性與確認。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為家庭相簿選章節，現有次序按年份，但祖母想先把同一地點的照片放一起試看。你願意試排、比較哪個容易講故事，尚未改正式檔。用一至兩句英文回應她。
writing.selfCheckZh: 肯定次序仍可改並提試排比較，保留正式檔未改，不把彈性變已批准或原本沒安排。

examples.en: The chapter order is not set in stone, so we can try grouping the photographs by place. Let’s compare that version before changing the main file.
examples.zh: 章節次序未固定，所以可試按地點組照片。改正式檔前，先比較該版吧。

examples.en: It is not set in stone; your idea is worth a trial. We can see which order makes the family stories easier to follow.
examples.zh: 它尚未固定；你的想法值得試。我們可看哪次序讓家族故事較易跟。

takeaways.en: The draft schedule was not set in stone, so we invited the group to suggest changes.
takeaways.zh: 草稿時間表未固定，所以我們請小組提改動。

takeaways.en: The agreement was treated as set in stone until both sides chose to review it.
takeaways.zh: 雙方選擇重檢前，協議被視作已固定。

brief.meaningEn: Figuratively fixed from the outset or deeply built in, as if wired into a machine.
brief.meaningZh: 比喻從一開始已固定或根深蒂固，彷彿接在機器線路中。
brief.grammar: preferences are/not necessarily hard-wired; attend to the scope of not necessarily rather than replacing it with a scientific claim.
brief.register: Electrical metaphor in descriptions of human preferences. This lesson interprets the wording, not biological evidence about an individual.
brief.boundaryZh: 說未必固定，不等於所有偏好可立即任改，也不由某次選擇證明天生或後天原因。
brief.misconceptionZh: 從變化可描述經驗差異，但不要用片語替未查的成因下結論。
brief.outcomeZh: 能準確理解固定程度與否定範圍，保留改變及原因的不確定性。

sources.sentence: Our tastes are not necessarily hard-wired.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 20, table 1, row 5; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: Our preferences are not necessarily hard-wired: I used to avoid long interviews, but after hearing a few engaging examples I began to enjoy them, without knowing exactly why my response changed.
listening.zh: 偏好未必一開始就固定：我以前避長訪談，聽幾個吸引例子後開始喜歡，但不確知反應為何改。
listening.promptZh: 這段經歷支持哪個有保留的說法？

options.en: The speaker’s preference changed, without establishing its exact cause.
options.zh: 說話者偏好改變，未確立確切原因。

options.en: The speaker’s preference had remained unchanged throughout.
options.zh: 說話者偏好一直不變。

options.en: The speaker has established the biological cause of this change in preference.
options.zh: 說話者已確立這次偏好改變的生物成因。

options.en: The speaker disliked all the interviews even after trying them.
options.zh: 說話者試後仍不喜歡所有訪談。

listening.explanationZh: 原先避開、後來喜歡顯示偏好變化；說話者不確知原因，未確立生物機制。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你不想把自己的訪談偏好說成一直固定？
reply.promptEn: Why would you avoid describing your interview preference as permanently fixed?

options.en: I once avoided long interviews but later began to enjoy some of them.
options.zh: 我曾避長訪談，後來開始喜歡其中一些。

options.en: My taste did not seem entirely hard-wired, given that change in response.
options.zh: 有那反應改變，我的喜好看來並非全固定。

options.en: The newer experience differed from my earlier expectation.
options.zh: 新體驗與早先預期不同。

options.en: I have evidence of a change in my own preference, though not a full explanation for it.
options.zh: 我有自身偏好改變的依據，卻未完整解釋原因。

reply.explanationZh: 四句給自身改變，不推全體或已知生物機制。

scene.promptZh: 同學以前不喜歡合唱，後來聽不同作品發現喜歡其中一種；你要描述這次經歷，不猜基因。哪句準確？

options.en: Her preference does not appear completely hard-wired; her response changed with the new experience.
options.zh: 她的偏好看來並非全固定；新體驗中反應改了。

options.en: The change establishes exactly how her genes control musical taste.
options.zh: 改變確立基因怎樣控制她音樂喜好。

options.en: Her earlier dislike remained unchanged after she tried the different works.
options.zh: 她試不同作品後，原先不喜歡仍沒變。

scene.explanationZh: 題目明說開始喜歡其中一種，支持本次反應改變；未推基因機制，也不是完全未變。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜從 tastes are not necessarily hard-wired 得出？

options.en: Some preferences may not be fixed from the beginning.
options.zh: 有些偏好未必一開始固定。

options.en: The speaker can deliberately reverse this preference immediately on request.
options.zh: 只要被要求，說話者便可立即刻意反轉這項偏好。

options.en: The sentence does not supply a complete explanation of how tastes develop.
options.zh: 句子未完整解釋喜好怎樣形成。

contrast.explanationZh: 未必固定不等於能按要求立即自行反轉；原因及可控制程度未有交代。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想用你由不喜歡轉喜歡訪談，解釋全班偏好的成因；你只有自己的經驗。哪句最好？

options.en: Describe my change and its limits before making claims about other people.
options.zh: 先描述我的改變及範圍，再談其他人的說法。

options.en: Use my change as proof that the whole class’s tastes have the same cause.
options.zh: 把我的改變當全班喜好有同一成因的證據。

options.en: Say my earlier dislike never existed because I enjoy some interviews now.
options.zh: 因我現喜歡部分訪談，就說早先不喜歡從未存在。

dialogue.explanationZh: 自身前後都可如實記，未能推出別人成因。

speaking.en: My preferences are not necessarily hard-wired, but one changed response does not explain everyone’s tastes.
speaking.zh: 我的偏好未必固定，但一次反應改變不解釋每個人喜好。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再保留固定程度與資料範圍。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你編閱讀問卷介紹，不想把同學第一次選的書當成永久標籤；你會隔一段時間再問，讓他們說明有沒有新喜好，也容許沒變。用一至兩句英文說明這個安排，不宣稱已知道偏好成因。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用重問安排避免首次選擇變永久標籤，容許變與不變，不把問卷當成因證明或強迫改喜好。

examples.en: We should not treat the first book choice as a hard-wired preference. A later question can let students describe a new interest or say that their choice has stayed the same.
examples.zh: 我們不應把首次選書當固定偏好。稍後再問，可讓學生描述新興趣，或說選擇未變。

examples.en: Rather than assume tastes are hard-wired, we will ask again after students have tried other books. Their replies can show change or continuity without explaining every cause.
examples.zh: 與其假定喜好固定，我們會在學生試其他書後再問。回覆可顯示變或不變，不代表解釋所有成因。

takeaways.en: I no longer treated my early dislike as a hard-wired preference after discovering other versions of the story.
takeaways.zh: 發現故事其他版本後，我不再把早先不喜歡當固定偏好。

takeaways.en: The survey did not show that those tastes were hard-wired; it recorded what people chose that month.
takeaways.zh: 問卷沒顯示喜好固定；它記錄人們當月選甚麼。

brief.meaningEn: Very full of people in the stated place or event.

brief.boundaryZh: 人多不直接證明滿意、學習成效、收益或場地安全；需另有相關資料。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要說清何處何時擠滿，不把某一刻擴成活動全程。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述人群密度，分開到場狀況與其他成效。

listening.en: The foyer was packed just before the doors opened, while the main hall was still being prepared; we had not yet collected any feedback on the event.
listening.zh: 開門前門廳擠滿人，主禮堂仍在準備；我們尚未收活動回饋。

options.en: The foyer at the point just before opening.
options.zh: 開門前那刻的門廳。

options.en: The main hall after every visitor had taken a seat.
options.zh: 每位訪客入座後的主禮堂。

options.en: The event’s feedback results after it finished.
options.zh: 活動結束後的回饋結果。

options.en: The entrance bags filled with event materials.
options.zh: 裝活動材料的入口提袋。

listening.explanationZh: foyer及just before定位場所時間，不是主場已坐好或意見已收。

reply.promptZh: 開門前，入口附近怎樣？
reply.promptEn: What was the entrance area like before opening?

options.en: The foyer was very crowded while the hall was still being prepared.
options.zh: 門廳很擠，禮堂仍在準備。

options.en: The foyer was packed just before opening.
options.zh: 開門前門廳擠滿人。

options.en: A large crowd had gathered in the entrance area at that point.
options.zh: 那刻一大群人在入口區聚集。

options.en: There was little free space among the people waiting in the foyer.
options.zh: 門廳等候人群之間沒多少空位。

reply.explanationZh: 四句描該刻門廳，不加滿意結論。

scene.promptZh: 市集午間的小走廊人挨着人，你只觀察這條走廊，還未到其他區。哪句準確？

options.en: This corridor is packed at lunchtime.
options.zh: 這走廊午間擠滿人。

options.en: The whole market is empty at this time.
options.zh: 整個市集此時無人。

options.en: Visitor satisfaction has already been confirmed from their comments.
options.zh: 已從意見確認訪客滿意。

scene.explanationZh: 局部密度可描述，未給全場空或回饋結果。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜單憑 the hall was packed 得出？

options.en: The hall was very full of people.
options.zh: 禮堂擠滿人。

options.en: The audience’s satisfaction has been established.
options.zh: 觀眾滿意程度已確立。

options.en: An exact attendance figure may require a separate count.
options.zh: 精確到場數可能另需點算。

contrast.explanationZh: 擠滿不是滿意調查。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問「門廳那麼多人，所以大家一定很喜歡活動？」但活動未開始。哪句較準確？

options.en: We can report the crowd, but we need later feedback to know how people felt about the event.
options.zh: 可報人群，但需之後回饋才知大家對活動感受。

options.en: The waiting crowd is already positive feedback on the performances.
options.zh: 等候人群已是對演出的正面回饋。

options.en: The account only counts people entering; it does not describe anyone waiting in the foyer.
options.zh: 敘述只點入場人數，沒描述有人在門廳等候。

dialogue.explanationZh: 門廳已觀察到等候人群，但活動未開始、意見未收；不能把等候直接當演出評價或抹去已見的人群。

speaking.en: The foyer was packed, but we had not yet heard how people felt about the event.
speaking.zh: 門廳擠滿人，但我們尚未聽活動感受。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清擠迫與回饋。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你要回報圖書館活動後的動線，茶點桌旁曾擠滿人，其他出口仍可用；你想請下次把取杯與取食物分開，先說觀察而非猜全場人數或滿意度。用一至兩句英文提出改善。
writing.selfCheckZh: 按局部排隊密度提出分流安排，保留其他出口狀況，不從擠滿補精確人數或滿意程度。

examples.en: The area beside the refreshments was packed after the talk, although the other exits remained available. We should separate the cups from the food next time to spread out the queue.
examples.zh: 講座後茶點旁擠滿人，其他出口仍可用。下次應把杯與食物分開，讓隊伍分散。

examples.en: People gathered so closely that the refreshment corner was packed. Moving the cups to a second table could make the next queue less concentrated.
examples.zh: 大家聚得很密，茶點角擠滿人。把杯移到另一桌，可讓下次隊伍不那麼集中。

takeaways.en: The small gallery was packed during the final hour of the exhibition.

takeaways.en: The entrance was packed, so we checked where the waiting visitors could stand.
takeaways.zh: 入口擠滿人，所以我們查等候訪客可站哪裏。

brief.meaningEn: Overly tidy categories that leave out the complexity or variety of real people or experiences.
brief.meaningZh: 過度整齊簡單的分類，忽略真人或經歷的複雜與多樣。
brief.grammar: put people into neat little boxes; people do not fit into neat little boxes; boxes are categories in this metaphor.
brief.register: Contextual container metaphor, often critical of rigid classification. Neat describes apparent simplicity, not physical tidiness here.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是所有分類都無用；問題是把多樣的人硬塞入排他、固定類別，忽略資料。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可為特定目的暫作分類，但要容許重疊、變化及個人說明。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出分類漏掉的差異，提出較靈活的描述。

listening.en: The reading survey’s neat little boxes did not fit Lina: she enjoyed both comic stories and detailed historical accounts, yet the form allowed only one permanent label.
listening.zh: 閱讀問卷簡單類別不合莉娜：她既喜歡漫畫故事，也喜歡詳盡歷史敘述，但表格只容一個永久標籤。

options.en: It forced a single fixed category despite overlapping interests.
options.zh: 興趣重疊，卻強制單一固定類別。

options.en: It let Lina describe both interests in her own words.
options.zh: 它讓莉娜用自己話描述兩種興趣。

options.en: It asked only for which book she had borrowed that day.
options.zh: 它只問她當天借哪本書。

options.en: It recorded her choices without assigning any label.
options.zh: 它記選擇，不加標籤。

listening.explanationZh: both興趣及only permanent label是分類過硬，不是開放描述或只記當日。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼這問卷不能準確描述莉娜？
reply.promptEn: Why does the survey fail to describe Lina accurately?

options.en: Her interests overlap, but the form requires one permanent category.
options.zh: 她興趣重疊，表格卻要永久單一類別。

options.en: The neat little boxes leave no room for her mix of comic and historical reading.
options.zh: 簡單類別沒留位置給她漫畫與歷史閱讀的組合。

options.en: She cannot show both interests through the single label available.
options.zh: 她不能用唯一標籤顯示兩種興趣。

options.en: The form makes a fixed division that her actual choices do not follow.
options.zh: 表格作固定區分，她實際選擇卻不跟。

reply.explanationZh: 四句給分類與資料不符的理由，不否定問閱讀本身。

scene.promptZh: 活動表把人只分「喜歡安靜」或「喜歡熱鬧」，但你會按場合選不同活動，想可多選並補說明。哪句準確？

options.en: These neat little boxes miss how my preferences change with the occasion.
options.zh: 這些簡單類別漏了我的偏好會隨場合變。

options.en: The current form already lets me choose both and explain the difference.
options.zh: 目前表格已讓我兩者都選並解釋差別。

options.en: My preference for one quiet event means I cannot enjoy a lively gathering.
options.zh: 我喜歡一次安靜活動，表示不能享受熱鬧聚會。

scene.explanationZh: 場合差異不合排他二選一，應保留實際變化。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不像本課批評的 neat little boxes？

options.en: A single permanent label that overrides overlapping interests.
options.zh: 壓過重疊興趣的單一永久標籤。

options.en: A flexible description that permits several interests and updates.
options.zh: 容許幾種興趣及更新的彈性描述。

options.en: A rigid division that ignores choices outside its categories.
options.zh: 忽略類別外選擇的僵硬區分。

contrast.explanationZh: 有彈性及可更新避免硬塞類別。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問「那是不是任何問卷分類都不能用？」你只想修這個排他的永久標籤。哪句最好？

options.en: Categories can help a limited purpose if people can show overlap and explain changes.
options.zh: 若可顯示重疊及解釋變化，分類能幫特定目的。

options.en: Yes, we should stop asking what readers enjoy because preferences can vary.
options.zh: 對，因偏好可變，就應停止問讀者喜歡甚麼。

options.en: Keep the permanent category and treat Lina’s second interest as a recording error.
options.zh: 保留永久類別，把莉娜第二興趣當記錯。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可改善設計而非全否定問卷，也不能以分類改資料。

speaking.en: People do not always fit into neat little boxes, so the form should leave room for mixed interests.
speaking.zh: 人不總能放進簡單類別，所以表格應留混合興趣空間。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把分類限制與設計連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替展覽把工藝作者標成「傳統」或「現代」，但一位作者用舊編織法製作新式燈罩。你想改標示，容許觀眾看技法與用途的組合，不硬說她只屬一類。用一至兩句英文提出建議。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用舊技法新用途的組合指出分類不足，提出具體標示，不由傳統現代名稱替作者定單一永久身分。

examples.en: The neat little boxes of traditional or modern miss how her old weaving method serves a new design. Let’s describe the technique and purpose together.
examples.zh: 傳統或現代的簡單類別，漏了她舊編織法如何服務新設計。把技法與用途一起描述吧。

examples.en: Rather than put the maker into neat little boxes, the label should explain how inherited skills appear in a contemporary lampshade.
examples.zh: 與其把作者硬分簡單類別，標示應解釋傳承技藝怎樣出現在當代燈罩。

takeaways.en: The interviews showed lives that did not fit into the survey’s neat little boxes.
takeaways.zh: 訪問顯示的生活，不符合問卷的簡單類別。

takeaways.en: We replaced the neat little boxes with a description that allowed more than one interest.
takeaways.zh: 我們以容許多種興趣的描述取代簡單類別。

brief.meaningEn: Hard, repetitive or boring everyday work and duties.
brief.meaningZh: 每天費力、重複或沉悶的工作及責任。
brief.grammar: relief from/return to the daily grind; the daily grind of + -ing/task; describe the repeated demand rather than a one-off exciting challenge.
brief.register: Established informal routine-work expression, supported by Cambridge daily grind. It describes the experience as tiring or monotonous, not the work’s moral value.
brief.boundaryZh: 有疲憊感不表示不負責任、工作沒價值或每段生活都沉悶；需說明哪種重複負荷。
brief.misconceptionZh: 一小段休息可舒緩，不等於日常任務已消失或必須放棄。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述重複日常帶來的感受，保留責任及短暫轉換。

listening.en: An evening walk gave me a brief break from the daily grind of checking the same stock lists and answering routine requests, before I returned to the notes I needed for tomorrow.
listening.zh: 晚間散步讓我暫離每天核同類存貨表、答例行請求的重複工作，之後再回明天所需筆記。

options.en: The repeated everyday checking and routine replies.
options.zh: 每天重複核對及例行回覆。

options.en: Only the new and unusual walking route that evening.
options.zh: 只有當晚新而特別的散步路線。

options.en: An announcement that tomorrow’s duties had been cancelled.
options.zh: 宣布明天責任已取消。

options.en: A single unexpected event unrelated to the normal tasks.
options.zh: 與平常任務無關的一次意外事件。

listening.explanationZh: same lists及routine requests說日常重複，briefbreak未取消明日工作。

reply.promptZh: 晚間散步讓你暫離甚麼？
reply.promptEn: What did the evening walk give you a break from?

options.en: The repeated stock checks and routine requests of the day.
options.zh: 當天重複核存貨及例行請求。

options.en: The daily grind of doing the same checks and replies.
options.zh: 每天重複核對回覆的費力日常。

options.en: A monotonous part of my usual responsibilities.
options.zh: 平常責任中沉悶重複的部分。

options.en: The routine work I would still need to prepare for again tomorrow.
options.zh: 明天仍需再準備的例行工作。

reply.explanationZh: 四句描述相同重複責任，不加取消或全無價值。

scene.promptZh: 你一連幾周每天整理同類表格，覺重複費神，周末讀故事能暫時換心情，之後仍回工作。哪句貼切？

options.en: The story offers a short escape from the daily grind.
options.zh: 故事讓人短暫離開費力重複日常。

options.en: The weekday tasks had been cancelled before the reading break began.
options.zh: 閱讀休息開始前，平日任務已取消。

options.en: The account is about a single surprising task rather than a repeated routine.
options.zh: 敘述關於一次驚喜任務，而非重複日常。

scene.explanationZh: 幾周每天同類整理支持費力日常；故事讓人暫時換心情，題目仍說之後回工作，不是已取消。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不像 the daily grind？

options.en: Repetitive duties experienced as tiring over time.
options.zh: 一段時間下來感到費力的重複責任。

options.en: A one-off novelty described as a refreshing change from usual work.
options.zh: 被描述為轉換日常、令人精神一振的一次新體驗。

options.en: Hard everyday tasks that offer little variety.
options.zh: 少變化的費力日常任務。

contrast.explanationZh: 一次新鮮轉換不是重複日常本身。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問「你想暫離日常，就表示完全不在乎工作？」但你仍準備明天筆記。哪句準確？

options.en: Wanting a brief change can coexist with taking tomorrow’s responsibilities seriously.
options.zh: 想短暫轉換，可與認真對待明日責任並存。

options.en: Yes, taking the walk was a decision to stop preparing for tomorrow.
options.zh: 對，去散步是決定停止明日準備。

options.en: The evening walk was another routine duty rather than a change from the usual work.
options.zh: 晚間散步是另一項例行責任，不是離開平常工作的轉換。

dialogue.explanationZh: 散步是短暫轉換，之後仍準備筆記；不能說已放棄工作，也不能把這次休息改作另一項例行任務。

speaking.en: The walk gave me a break from the daily grind, not a reason to ignore the work waiting for tomorrow.
speaking.zh: 散步讓我暫離費力日常，不是忽略明日工作的理由。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清暫時轉換與責任。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替社區創作小組寫每周聚會邀請，成員常做重複家務或文書，聚會讓大家一小時試簡單拼貼、換換心情，不承諾解決生活所有壓力。用一至兩句英文邀請他們。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以一小時創作邀請短暫轉換，不承諾所有負荷消失，也不把聚會變必須產出作品的另一工作。

examples.en: Join us for an hour of collage and a change from the daily grind. You do not need a finished artwork; we will simply try materials and share ideas.
examples.zh: 來用一小時拼貼，換換費力日常吧。不需完成作品；我們只試材料、分享想法。

examples.en: The group offers a small break from the daily grind through a relaxed creative session, with room to return to everyday duties afterwards.
examples.zh: 小組以輕鬆創作讓人短暫離開重複日常，之後仍可回各自責任。

takeaways.en: A short conversation about a favourite book offered relief from the daily grind.
takeaways.zh: 談一會喜歡的書，讓費力日常稍有舒緩。

takeaways.en: She returned to the daily grind after the weekend, carrying a few ideas from the workshop.

brief.meaningEn: Make progress with an activity, decision or development plan, especially after a difficulty or delay; moving ahead quickly describes its pace, not completed success.
brief.meaningZh: 推進活動、決定或發展計劃，尤指經困難或延誤後；move ahead quickly 說明進展速度，不表示已完成。
brief.grammar: Move forward with a plan; moved in the past; can move forward once a condition is met. For a city or project, move ahead quickly with new rail lines or similar transport development describes rapid progress, not a train physically moving. The plan supplies the figurative direction.
brief.register: Common figurative progress use. A team lead may tell colleagues a rehearsal can move forward after a timing issue, while a planner may tell residents a rail project is moving ahead quickly after approvals.
brief.boundaryZh: 推進或進展快不等於已完成、問題全解或必定成功；辨清具體已走的一步及未完成部分。
brief.misconceptionZh: 一次進展可以很實際，仍可有待查資料及後續工作。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出推進的是哪一步，保留條件及未完成部分。

contrast.explanationZh: 進展與全部完成不同。

titleEn: serve both the head and the heart

target.pattern: \bserv(?:e|es|ed|ing) both the head and the heart\b

brief.meaningEn: Satisfy or engage both thought and feeling.
brief.meaningZh: 同時滿足或引發思考與情感。
brief.grammar: a work serves both the head and the heart; served in past; head represents thought, heart represents feeling in this paired image.
brief.register: Expressive body-based pairing, not a literal account of organs or a fixed division between types of people.
brief.boundaryZh: 兼顧兩者不保證內容真實、人人都喜歡或兩方面一樣強；需給思考及感受各自依據。
brief.misconceptionZh: 有情感可仍需查資料，有資訊亦可觸動，不把兩者當互相排斥。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體認知及情感效果支持兼顧的評價。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.expression: serves both the head and the heart
sources.sentence: A good novel serves both the head and the heart.

listening.en: The exhibition served both the head and the heart: its clear timeline helped us understand the decisions, while the recorded voices made the separations feel personal.
listening.zh: 展覽兼顧思考及情感：清楚時間線幫理解決定，錄音聲音則讓離別有個人感。
listening.promptZh: 哪兩種效果支持這個評價？

options.en: Understanding decisions and feeling the personal impact of separation.
options.zh: 理解決定，並感受離別的個人影響。

options.en: Only checking dates, with no emotional response described.
options.zh: 只有核日期，沒描述情感反應。

options.en: Only feeling moved, with no structure helping understanding.
options.zh: 只有感動，沒結構幫理解。

options.en: Receiving a complete proof that every recording was factually accurate.
options.zh: 獲完整證據，證明每段錄音事實準確。

listening.explanationZh: timeline與voices分別支援理解及感受，不保證所有錄音已核。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼說展覽既有思考也有情感？
reply.promptEn: Why do you say the exhibition engaged both thought and feeling?

options.en: The timeline explained the decisions, and the voices made the separations personal.
options.zh: 時間線解釋決定，聲音讓離別有個人感。

options.en: It served both the head and the heart through clear context and personal voices.
options.zh: 它透過清楚背景及個人聲音兼顧思考情感。

options.en: We could follow the choices and feel what they meant to people.
options.zh: 我們可跟選擇，也感到它們對人的意義。

options.en: The structure aided understanding while the recordings carried feeling.
options.zh: 結構助理解，錄音帶情感。

reply.explanationZh: 四句皆有認知及感受兩部分，不只空泛稱好。

scene.promptZh: 故事用清楚因果讓你思考責任，又用朋友離別的對話觸動你；你仍對部分選擇有疑問。哪句準確？

options.en: It serves both the head and the heart without settling every question for me.
options.zh: 它兼顧思考情感，卻沒替我解每個問題。

options.en: I understood the reasoning about responsibility but had no emotional response to the farewell.
options.zh: 我理解責任的推理，但對離別沒情感反應。

options.en: The farewell moved me, but the characters’ reasons remained impossible to understand.
options.zh: 離別令我感動，但角色理由仍無法理解。

scene.explanationZh: 題目同時給清楚因果引發思考、離別對話觸動感受；只說其中一面與已給經驗不符，仍可保留疑問。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 serves both the head and the heart？

options.en: Clear explanation together with a personal emotional connection.
options.zh: 清楚解釋加個人情感連結。

options.en: A list of facts with no described feeling or human connection.
options.zh: 一份資料表，未描述感受或人際連結。

options.en: A work that prompts questions and evokes sympathy.
options.zh: 引發問題及同情的作品。

contrast.explanationZh: 只有認知資料，未足支持兩方面都兼顧。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說「有聲音感動，就不需時間線資料」，但兩者在這展覽各有作用。哪句較準確？

options.en: Keep the emotional voices and the context that helps us understand their choices.
options.zh: 保留情感聲音及幫理解選擇的背景。

options.en: The recordings can replace the dates and decisions even when those explain the story.
options.zh: 即使日期決定解釋故事，錄音仍可全取代它們。

options.en: Only the timeline matters, since the personal voices do not contribute to thought.
options.zh: 只有時間線重要，因個人聲音對思考無貢獻。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可互補，不能只憑一面刪另一面。

speaking.en: The account serves both the head and the heart by explaining the choices and letting us hear their personal impact.
speaking.zh: 敘述解釋選擇，也讓人聽見個人影響，兼顧思考情感。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再給兩方面具體依據。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替朋友看一封道歉草稿，事實及下一步寫得清楚，卻沒承認漏傳訊息令對方不安。你想建議保留清楚解釋，並加一句真誠承認影響，不編感受或誇張承諾。用一至兩句英文給建議。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以清楚事實下一步支援理解、承認已知影響回應感受，不用情感取代交代或加入不實承諾。

examples.en: The letter can serve both the head and the heart by explaining the missed update and acknowledging the worry it caused. Keep the clear next step and add that honest recognition.
examples.zh: 信可解釋漏更新，也承認造成的不安，兼顧思考情感。保留清楚下一步，再加真誠承認吧。

examples.en: To serve both the head and the heart, the apology needs a clear account as well as recognition of the other person’s experience. It need not promise more than you can do.
examples.zh: 為兼顧思考情感，道歉需清楚交代，也承認對方經驗。不需承諾超過能力的事。

takeaways.en: The short film served both the head and the heart through its careful explanation and moving interviews.
takeaways.zh: 短片透過仔細解釋及動人訪問，兼顧思考情感。

takeaways.en: We wanted the guide to serve both the head and the heart, with clear context as well as personal memories.
takeaways.zh: 我們想指南兼顧思考情感，有清楚背景，也有個人回憶。

titleZh: 在共同閱讀空間中並存

brief.meaningEn: Coexist in a shared reading space or culture, using the shelf as a meeting place for different works.
brief.meaningZh: 以書架作相遇意象，描述不同作品在共同閱讀空間或文化中並存。
brief.grammar: local and translated stories meet on the same shelf; met in past; works are personified as meeting.
brief.register: Creative image from the guide. A literal shelf can support the broader image of works sharing a reading culture; not a fixed dictionary idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 並存不等於內容相同、銷量相同或文化差異消失；要保留各作品來源及特點。
brief.misconceptionZh: 共同接觸空間可讓人比較，不必把不同傳統合成單一聲音。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描寫作品共享位置又保留差異，提出有內容的並讀。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Local and translated stories meet on the same shelf in our library.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 21, table 1, row 2; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: In the club’s display, local and translated stories met on the same shelf, with short notes inviting readers to compare how each writer described leaving home.
listening.zh: 社團展示中，本地與翻譯故事在同一書架相遇，短註邀讀者比較各作者怎樣寫離家。
listening.promptZh: 相遇意象在此強調甚麼？

options.en: Different stories share a reading space and an opportunity for comparison.
options.zh: 不同故事共享閱讀空間及比較機會。

options.en: The stories have become identical translations of one original.
options.zh: 故事已變成同一原作的相同翻譯。

options.en: The translated stories replaced the local ones rather than being displayed alongside them.
options.zh: 翻譯故事取代本地故事，不是並列展示。

options.en: The notes keep local and translated books apart with no comparison.
options.zh: 短註把本地翻譯書隔開，不作比較。

listening.explanationZh: 本地及翻譯故事共同展示並邀比較，保留不同聲音，不是同一原作、互相取代或完全隔開。

reply.promptZh: 這個展示怎樣把兩類故事放在一起？
reply.promptEn: How does the display bring the two kinds of stories together?

options.en: It invites readers to compare local and translated accounts of leaving home.
options.zh: 它邀讀者比較本地及翻譯離家敘述。

options.en: The stories meet on the same shelf while keeping their different voices.
options.zh: 故事在共同書架相遇，同時保留不同聲音。

options.en: A shared display gives readers a way to explore both kinds together.
options.zh: 共同展示給讀者一起探索兩類的途徑。

options.en: The notes connect a shared theme with the writers’ different descriptions.
options.zh: 短註把共同主題與各作者不同描寫連起來。

reply.explanationZh: 四句描述共同接觸與比較，不強說全相同。

scene.promptZh: 你在網上共讀清單並列不同地方的故事，沒有實體書架，但保留作者及翻譯來源，邀大家比較離家的不同寫法。你想用創意書架意象描述這共同閱讀空間。哪句準確？

options.en: These stories meet on the same shelf in our online list, with their distinct voices and sources still clear.
options.zh: 這些故事在網上清單的共同書架相遇，仍清楚保留不同聲音及來源。

options.en: Without a physical shelf, the online list cannot offer any shared reading space for the stories.
options.zh: 沒有實體書架，網上清單便不能為故事提供共同閱讀空間。

options.en: The shared list presents the stories as versions of one text, with the same author and source.
options.zh: 共同清單把故事呈現為同一文本的版本，作者來源相同。

scene.explanationZh: 本課書架是共享閱讀空間的創意比喻，可用於網上清單；並列不會抹去各自作者來源或令它們變同一文本。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 meet on the same shelf 的比喻得出？

options.en: Different works coexist in a shared reading setting.
options.zh: 不同作品在共同閱讀環境並存。

options.en: Their cultural differences have necessarily disappeared.
options.zh: 它們的文化差異必定消失。

options.en: The context can explain the theme connecting them.
options.zh: 情境可解釋連起它們的主題。

contrast.explanationZh: 並存不消除差異。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把並讀說成幾位作者觀點完全一樣，但短註其實邀比較不同描寫。哪句較準確？

options.en: Keep the shared theme and show how the descriptions differ.
options.zh: 保留共同主題，顯示描寫怎樣不同。

options.en: The fact they share a display is enough to treat the voices as interchangeable.
options.zh: 共享展示已足以把聲音當可互換。

options.en: Put the leaving-home stories into separate displays with no shared-theme link.
options.zh: 把離家故事分成互不以共同主題連結的展示。

dialogue.explanationZh: 共同主題讓不同描寫可比較，不需把聲音當可互換，也不需為保留差異就取消連結。

speaking.en: The stories meet on the same shelf, giving us a chance to compare rather than erase their differences.
speaking.zh: 故事在共同書架相遇，給我們比較而非抹差異的機會。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再保留並存與差異。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為家族閱讀角寫卡片，祖母原語言的童話與你的中文譯本會放在一起，方便兩代互相讀一段並談不同用詞。你想介紹這個共同閱讀安排，仍保留原作者及譯者署名。用一至兩句英文寫卡片。
writing.selfCheckZh: 交代雙語並讀及兩代交流的實際用途，保留署名及用詞差異，不把共同書架當版本相同或互相取代。

examples.en: The original tale and our translation meet on the same shelf so two generations can read a passage together. The card will name both the author and the translator.

examples.en: Here the two versions meet on the same shelf, inviting us to share the story and discuss the different words. Neither version needs to replace the other.

takeaways.en: Old and new accounts meet on the same shelf, ready for readers to compare.

takeaways.en: The two traditions met on the same shelf without becoming one voice.

titleZh: 日常活動的節奏與模式

brief.meaningEn: The recurring pattern, timing or pace of an activity, beyond literal musical rhythm.
brief.meaningZh: 活動反覆出現的模式、時間安排或快慢，超出實際音樂節拍。
brief.grammar: the rhythm of family life/work/a routine; identify which repeated activities create the pattern.
brief.register: Conventional musical metaphor for everyday patterns. This lesson focuses on household or work routines, not a measured heartbeat or musical metre.
brief.boundaryZh: 節奏改變不自動表示較好較差、人人相同或原有習慣全消失；要指出實際時間或活動關聯。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不只用快慢空泛形容，應說明哪個安排令活動如何接續。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把時間安排連到反覆生活模式，保留個別影響。

listening.en: The earlier library opening changed the rhythm of our family mornings: we could return books on the way to school rather than make a separate trip after dinner.
listening.zh: 圖書館提早開門，改變我們家庭早晨節奏：可上學途中還書，不需晚飯後另去一趟。

options.en: Returning books became part of the school journey instead of a separate evening trip.
options.zh: 還書成上學路程一部分，不再另作晚間行程。

options.en: The library visit still took place after dinner without any timing change.
options.zh: 圖書館到訪仍在晚餐後，時間沒改。

options.en: Every family adopted the same new routine.
options.zh: 每個家庭都採同一新日常。

options.en: The account measured the speed of music played in the library.
options.zh: 敘述量圖書館音樂速度。

listening.explanationZh: 早開讓還書嵌入上學路線，非所有家庭或音樂。

reply.promptEn: How did the earlier opening affect your family mornings?

options.en: We could combine the book return with the trip to school.
options.zh: 我們可把還書與上學路程合併。

options.en: It changed the rhythm of our mornings by moving the library trip into the school journey.
options.zh: 它把圖書館行程移入上學途中，改變早晨節奏。

options.en: A task once done after dinner fitted into the morning route.
options.zh: 原在晚飯後做的任務，可放入早晨路線。

options.en: We no longer needed a separate evening visit to return the books.
options.zh: 還書不再需另作晚間到訪。

reply.explanationZh: 四句給具體安排變化，不代其他家庭。

scene.promptZh: 工作坊把短討論集中在開頭，之後有一段不被打斷的製作時間；你想描述活動接續改變。哪句準確？

options.en: The new order changed the rhythm of the workshop.
options.zh: 新次序改變工作坊節奏。

options.en: The schedule changed only the music’s beat and left the activity order untouched.
options.zh: 時間表只改音樂節拍，活動次序不變。

options.en: The discussion and making time were both removed.
options.zh: 討論及製作時間都被移除。

scene.explanationZh: 開頭討論後連續做，支持活動模式而非音樂或全刪。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以解釋活動 the rhythm of 的比喻？

options.en: A regular sequence of meetings followed by uninterrupted work.
options.zh: 定期會議後接不受打斷工作的次序。

options.en: A literal musical beat with no relation to the activity’s schedule.
options.zh: 與活動時間表無關的實際音樂節拍。

options.en: A daily task moved to a different part of a routine.
options.zh: 日常任務移到日程另一部分。

contrast.explanationZh: 本課指活動模式，只有實際節拍未說明該模式。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問「你家早晨改了，是否代表人人生活都更輕鬆？」你只知自己的還書路程。哪句較準確？

options.en: Describe our combined trip and check other families’ arrangements before making a wider claim.
options.zh: 描述我們合併行程，作更廣說法前先查別家安排。

options.en: Yes, our morning route records the effect on all households.
options.zh: 對，我們早晨路線記錄所有家庭影響。

options.en: Our family still makes a separate return trip after dinner as well as the school journey.
options.zh: 我們家除了上學路程，晚餐後仍另去一趟還書。

dialogue.explanationZh: 我們已把還書併進上學路程，省去原晚間一趟；可報自己的改變，但未代表其他家庭都如此。

speaking.en: The new arrangement changed the rhythm of our work by grouping the check-ins before a quiet writing period.
speaking.zh: 新安排把聯絡集中在安靜寫作前，改變工作節奏。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再用接續安排支持比喻。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們拍地方短片，清晨街道較安靜且有斜光，適合外景，午間則回室內剪素材及整理聲音；天氣變會再調。你想給新組員說明拍攝日的活動節奏及原因，不只列同一時段開會。用一至兩句英文交接。

examples.en: The rhythm of our filming day follows the light and the street noise: we shoot outside early and work on the footage indoors at midday. We will adjust if the weather changes.
examples.zh: 拍攝日節奏跟着光線及街聲：早上外拍，午間室內處理素材；天氣變會調整。

examples.en: Morning location work and midday editing shape the rhythm of the filming day. The early quiet helps us capture the street, while the indoor period lets us review what we have recorded.
examples.zh: 早上外景及午間剪輯塑造拍攝日節奏；清晨安靜有助記錄街道，室內時段讓我們檢視已錄內容。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以光線及街聲解釋外拍、室內剪素材的活動交替，保留天氣可調，不把節奏只當音樂或固定不能變的鐘點。

takeaways.en: The later opening changed the rhythm of the studio day, with preparation now taking place before visitors arrived.
takeaways.zh: 較後開門改變工作室日程節奏，準備現可在訪客到前進行。

takeaways.en: We noticed the rhythm of family life shift when the school timetable changed.
takeaways.zh: 學校時間表改時，我們留意到家庭生活節奏轉變。

options.en: I lifted a printed card without learning what the term meant.
options.zh: 我只拿起卡，沒學術語意思。

options.en: I completed the full technical vocabulary course before hearing the term.
options.zh: 我聽術語前已完成全套專門詞彙課。

scene.explanationZh: 聽、留意意思及試用支持自然學到，不是拿卡或已上全課。

listening.en: The journeys differed, but the common thread in the three accounts was help from a stranger: one person found a lost bag, another explained a route, and a third offered a place to wait.
listening.zh: 旅途不同，但三份敘述共同主題是陌生人幫助：有人找失袋、有人解路線、另有人給地方等候。

options.en: Help from a stranger in different practical forms.
options.zh: 以不同實際形式出現的陌生人幫助。

options.zh: 共同主題是獲不熟悉的人實際幫助。

options.en: The lost bag, route and waiting place each showed an act of assistance.
options.zh: 失袋、路線及等候地方，各顯示一次幫助。

options.en: Their connection was the help offered, not an identical journey.
options.zh: 相連的是所獲幫助，不是完全相同旅程。

reply.explanationZh: 四句給共同主題且保留各種形式。

scene.promptZh: 三位創作者用不同媒介，都說反覆修改讓作品更清楚；你想概括這點，不說創作方法全一樣。哪句準確？

options.en: A common thread is learning through revision, despite the different media.
options.zh: 儘管媒介不同，共同主題是從修改中學。

options.en: They all used the same medium and followed one identical process.
options.zh: 他們都用同一媒介、同一程序。

options.en: The accounts share no idea because their materials differ.
options.zh: 因材料不同，敘述就沒有共同想法。

scene.explanationZh: 修改學習可跨不同媒介連結，不抹差異也不否認共同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 a common thread links the accounts 得出？

options.en: A supported theme connects the accounts.
options.zh: 一個有支持的主題連起敘述。

options.en: The accounts must match in all their details and causes.
options.zh: 敘述所有細節及原因都必定相同。

options.en: Individual differences can remain important.
options.zh: 個別差異仍可重要。

contrast.explanationZh: 連結一點不把全部相同化。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把三份旅途都寫成「找回失袋」，但只有一份是；你要保留共同幫助又不改事件。哪句最好？

options.en: Use help from a stranger as the link and keep the different actions in each account.
options.zh: 以陌生人幫助作連結，保留各敘述不同動作。

options.en: All three journeys involved recovering a lost bag, so that is the shared event.
options.zh: 三段旅程都涉及找回失袋，所以那是共同事件。

options.en: Drop the waiting-place account because its help did not involve a bag or a route.
options.zh: 因等候地方幫助沒涉及袋或路線，就棄該敘述。

dialogue.explanationZh: 只有一份失袋，其他是指路及提供等候地方；共同的是幫助，不需改事件或排掉符合的例子。

speaking.en: The common thread is mutual support, though the situations and actions differ.
speaking.zh: 共同主題是互相支持，儘管情況及行動不同。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再保留共同與差異。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替班級三篇反思寫導言，一篇學聆聽、一篇練解說、一篇調整設計，都提到同伴具體回饋讓自己發現盲點。你想用共同主題引讀，再讓每篇保留本身重點。用一至兩句英文寫導言。
writing.selfCheckZh: 以三篇都有的具體回饋與盲點作導言連結，保留各自任務及改變，不把共同主題變相同作品。

examples.en: The common thread in these reflections is learning from specific feedback, whether the task involved listening, explaining or designing. Each writer shows a different change in practice.
examples.zh: 這些反思共同主題，是從具體回饋學習，不論任務涉及聆聽、解說或設計。各作者顯示不同實踐改變。

examples.en: A common thread connects the three pieces: a colleague’s comment helped each writer notice a blind spot. The following accounts show how they responded in different ways.
examples.zh: 三篇由共同主題連起：同伴意見幫各作者留意盲點。以下敘述顯示他們怎樣以不同方式回應。

takeaways.en: A common thread in the interviews was the wish to make newcomers feel included.
takeaways.zh: 訪問共同主題，是想讓新人感到被接納。

takeaways.en: We identified the common thread without treating the different experiences as interchangeable.
takeaways.zh: 我們找共同主題，沒有把不同經歷當可互換。

english.evidence: Read every model, option and example for sense, grammar, contextual fit and target morphology; not independent human approval.

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese translations checked against each English sentence; not independent human approval.

brief.meaningEn: Be received positively by the people concerned.
brief.meaningZh: 獲相關人群正面接受或反應。
brief.grammar: an idea went down well with + group; should go down well predicts reception, not confirmed feedback; very strengthens degree.
brief.register: Common informal reaction phrase, especially British. This lesson concerns reception, not physical movement downwards.
brief.boundaryZh: 反應好不等於每人同意、必有長遠成效或已正式批准；should/may 仍是預計。
brief.misconceptionZh: 須分清實際回饋及說話者預測，並交代向誰反應好。
brief.outcomeZh: 能根據回饋或有保留預測描述接受程度。

listening.en: The shorter welcome should go down well with visitors who asked for more time to explore, but we will collect their comments after trying it on Saturday.
listening.zh: 較短歡迎環節應會獲想多些探索時間的訪客好評，但周六試後才收意見。

options.en: A supported expectation, with comments still to be collected after a trial.
options.zh: 有依據的預計，試後仍待收意見。

options.en: A completed survey confirming Saturday’s response.
options.zh: 已完成調查確認周六反應。

options.en: A report that visitors had asked for a longer welcome.
options.zh: 報告訪客要求更長歡迎環節。

options.en: An announcement that the trial had already been cancelled.
options.zh: 宣布試行已取消。

listening.explanationZh: should是預計，先前要求多探索時間是理由，will collect保留未試。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你預計短歡迎環節會受歡迎？
reply.promptEn: Why do you expect the shorter welcome to be received positively?

options.en: Visitors had asked for more time to explore.
options.zh: 訪客曾要求更多探索時間。

options.en: It should go down well because it responds to that request for extra time.
options.zh: 它回應多些時間的請求，所以應獲好反應。

options.en: The change leaves more of the session for what those visitors wanted to do.
options.zh: 改動讓環節有更多時間做那些訪客想做的事。

options.en: Their earlier comments support the idea, though the new version still needs testing.
options.zh: 先前意見支持想法，雖然新版仍需試。

reply.explanationZh: 四句給預計理由，不稱試後已知。

scene.promptZh: 試行新版路線圖後，受訪者說較易找路，並願下次再用；你只描述這批回饋。哪句準確？

options.en: The revised map went down well with the people we asked.
options.zh: 新版地圖獲我們所問的人好反應。

options.en: The positive response was predicted before the map was tried, with no comments yet.
options.zh: 地圖未試前預計正面，尚無意見。

options.en: The trial showed that nobody could follow the revised map.
options.zh: 試行顯示沒人能跟新版圖。

scene.explanationZh: 已有受訪者肯定支持實際反應，不是仍預測或無法用。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 should go down well 得出？

options.en: The speaker expects a positive reception.
options.zh: 說話者預計正面接受。

options.en: The audience’s actual reaction has already been confirmed.
options.zh: 觀眾實際反應已確認。

options.en: The reason for the expectation can be explained separately.
options.zh: 可另行解釋預期理由。

contrast.explanationZh: should預期不同於已收回饋。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問「你說應受歡迎，可以當作周六意見已收嗎？」但試行還未開始。哪句準確？

options.en: Call it an expectation and wait for the trial comments before reporting the result.
options.zh: 稱為預期，試行意見收後才報結果。

options.en: Yes, the earlier request is the same as feedback on the new version.
options.zh: 對，先前請求等同對新版的回饋。

options.en: No, we have no basis for considering a shorter welcome at all.
options.zh: 不，我們完全沒有考慮較短歡迎的依據。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先前請求可支持提議，不等於新版本已試。

speaking.en: The change should go down well, but I want to hear the actual feedback before calling it a success.
speaking.zh: 改動應會受歡迎，但稱成功前我想先聽實際回饋。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清預期與實績。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你試讀一封致謝訊息，兩位義工說最喜歡具體提及他們做過的事，而非籠統讚美。你想向小組建議用具體版本寄出，並把試讀反應限於這兩人，不聲稱全體已回覆。用一至兩句英文表達。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用兩人具體試讀反應支持版本選擇，保留小樣本及內容核對，不擴成已得全體反應。

examples.en: The specific thank-you went down well with the two volunteers who read the draft. We should use that version while keeping the tasks and names accurate.
examples.zh: 具體致謝獲試讀草稿的兩位義工好反應。我們應用該版，同時確保任務姓名準確。

examples.en: The draft went down very well in our small check because it named what people had actually done. That supports sending a precise message, not a claim that everyone has responded.
examples.zh: 小型試讀中，草稿具體說人們做過甚麼，所以很受歡迎。這支持寄準確訊息，不是聲稱人人已回覆。

takeaways.en: The clear explanation went down well with the new members.
takeaways.zh: 清楚解釋獲新成員好反應。

takeaways.en: The proposal had gone down very well, but the team still needed formal approval to begin.
takeaways.zh: 提案很受歡迎，但團隊仍需正式批准才開始。

english.evidence: Read every model, option and example for sense, grammar, contextual fit and target morphology; not independent human approval.

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese translations checked against each English sentence; not independent human approval.

brief.meaningEn: Maintain an advantage over other organisations or people competing in the same area.
brief.meaningZh: 在同一領域競爭中，維持相對其他人或機構的優勢。
brief.grammar: stay ahead of competitors by + -ing; stayed/staying; name the dimension of advantage when possible.
brief.register: Natural comparison using a race-position metaphor. This lesson is competitive performance, not literal distance along a road.
brief.boundaryZh: 領先要有比較及方面，不表示每項最好、永遠領先或競爭者消失；行動目的是領先不等於已達成。
brief.misconceptionZh: 新做法可為保持優勢而設計，仍需查顧客或表現反應。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分領先目標、具體做法與已觀察結果。

sources.sentence: Small firms must innovate to stay ahead of competitors.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 21, table 2, row 3; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The workshop introduced quicker appointment replies to stay ahead of competitors, but it was still tracking whether customers found the new process more useful.
listening.zh: 工作室為保持領先競爭者，引入較快預約回覆，但仍追蹤客人是否覺新程序較有用。
listening.promptZh: 新回覆安排的地位是甚麼？

options.en: A strategy for maintaining an advantage, with customer usefulness still under review.
options.zh: 保持優勢的策略，客人是否覺有用仍待檢視。

options.en: A measured comparison has already shown the workshop’s replies outperform competitors.
options.zh: 已有量度比較顯示工作室回覆勝過競爭者。

options.en: A decision to reply more slowly than before.
options.zh: 比以前更慢回覆的決定。

options.en: Customer feedback on the changed reply process has already been fully collected.
options.zh: 關於新回覆程序的顧客意見已全收齊。

listening.explanationZh: 較快回覆是保持優勢的策略，仍追蹤客人是否覺有用；未給已完成的競爭比較或意見調查。

reply.promptZh: 工作室為甚麼改快預約回覆？
reply.promptEn: Why did the workshop speed up appointment replies?

options.en: It wanted to maintain an advantage in service.
options.zh: 它想在服務上維持優勢。

options.en: It aimed to stay ahead of competitors by replying more quickly.
options.zh: 它想透過更快回覆保持領先競爭者。

options.en: The team hoped a more responsive process would help its competitive position.
options.zh: 團隊希望更快回應程序幫競爭地位。

options.en: It was trying to keep its service attractive while checking customers’ responses.
options.zh: 它嘗試保持服務吸引，同時查客人反應。

reply.explanationZh: 四句說目的，不把改善意圖當已確認成效。

scene.promptZh: 故事中兩個設計隊連續兩輪做同一批辨識題，甲隊都錯較少，仍想下一輪維持這個準確度優勢；尚未比較作品美感。哪句準確描述有證據的範圍？

options.en: The team wants to stay ahead of competitors in accuracy after making fewer errors in both rounds.
options.zh: 兩輪都錯較少後，團隊想繼續在準確度領先競爭者。

options.en: The two rounds have established that the team’s designs are also more attractive.
options.zh: 兩輪已確立團隊設計也更美觀。

options.en: The team is trying to recover an accuracy lead it lost in both measured rounds.
options.zh: 團隊正想追回在兩輪量度中都失去的準確度領先。

scene.explanationZh: 兩輪錯較少支持已有準確度優勢及想維持；不能轉成美感已比較，也不是兩輪都落後。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 a plan to stay ahead of competitors 得出？

options.en: The plan aims to maintain a competitive advantage.
options.zh: 計劃想維持競爭優勢。

options.en: The plan has already produced the intended advantage.
options.zh: 計劃已產生預期優勢。

options.en: The relevant measures and results still need describing.
options.zh: 仍需描述相關做法及結果。

contrast.explanationZh: 目的與實際成效不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問「回覆快了，所以顧客肯定都更滿意？」但團隊還在追蹤意見。哪句最好？

options.en: We can report the faster process and its aim, then check what customers actually say.
options.zh: 可報較快程序及目的，再查客人實際說甚麼。

options.en: The usefulness review is finished, so we can report the new reply process as preferred.
options.zh: 有用程度檢視已完，所以可報新回覆程序較受喜愛。

options.en: We should wait for a competitor to change its service before testing any change of our own.
options.zh: 應等競爭者先改服務，才測自己的任何改動。

dialogue.explanationZh: 團隊已引入回覆改動、仍追蹤意見，可報現況再查效果；不是檢視已完，也不需等對手先行。

speaking.en: We are trying to stay ahead of competitors, but we still need evidence of how the change works.
speaking.zh: 我們想保持領先競爭者，但仍需改動效果的證據。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分清目的與結果。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：友校辯論練習中，你們上輪的資料運用略有優勢，但對手這輪用了新報告。你想保持優勢，請同伴一起查新資料與自己論證仍未答的問題，不只增加投影片或保證取勝。用一至兩句英文向隊員建議。
writing.selfCheckZh: 用對手新資料說明需持續查證，提出分讀比較的具體準備，不把過去優勢當保證，也不以投影片數代證據。

examples.en: To stay ahead of competitors, we should examine the new reports and check the questions our argument has not answered. More slides alone will not keep our evidence strong.
examples.zh: 為保持領先競爭者，我們應查新報告及論證未答的問題。只加投影片，不能讓證據保持有力。

examples.en: We want to stay ahead of competitors by updating and checking our evidence, not by assuming last round’s advantage will remain. Let’s divide the reports and compare what they support.
examples.zh: 我們想更新核對證據以保持優勢，不假定上輪優勢會持續。分開讀報告，再比較支持甚麼吧。

takeaways.en: The team improved its support process to stay ahead of competitors.
takeaways.zh: 團隊改善支援程序，以保持領先競爭者。

takeaways.en: Staying ahead of competitors required checking which changes customers actually valued.
takeaways.zh: 保持領先競爭者需查客人實際重視哪些改動。

english.evidence: Read every model, option and example for sense, grammar, contextual fit and target morphology; not independent human approval.

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese translations checked against each English sentence; not independent human approval.

brief.meaningEn: Grow rapidly as one effect adds to another, like a rolling snowball gathering snow.
brief.meaningZh: 像滾雪球越滾越大，一個影響再加另一個，使事情迅速擴大。
brief.grammar: a problem snowballs into + larger result; snowballed/snowballing; can also describe positive growth if context supports it.
brief.register: Established figurative growth verb. The important idea is accumulating effects, not merely something already being large.
brief.boundaryZh: 不一定負面、沒有轉圜或永遠加大；需指出累積途徑及已知程度。
brief.misconceptionZh: 一個小問題未必必然成災，應分開可能、已發生及介入後改變。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述連鎖擴大的具體過程，保留可能與實際結果。

listening.en: The late script update snowballed into more work: the team first changed the captions, then had to rerecord two lines and check the timing again.
listening.zh: 劇本更新遲了，連鎖變更多工作：團隊先改字幕，再需重錄兩句、重查時間。

options.en: One change generated further connected tasks.
options.zh: 一項改動引出更多相關工作。

options.en: The extra work was already complete before the update arrived.
options.zh: 更新來前，額外工作已完成。

options.en: The update stayed limited to a spelling change with no further effect.
options.zh: 更新只限拼字，沒有後續影響。

options.en: The account measured a physical ball of snow.
options.zh: 敘述量實際雪球。

listening.explanationZh: 字幕、重錄、核時間串連，是累積效應。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼遲來更新帶來較多工作？
reply.promptEn: Why did the late update lead to more work?

options.en: Changing the captions led to rerecording and another timing check.
options.zh: 改字幕引出重錄及另一次核時間。

options.en: It snowballed as each change created another task.
options.zh: 每次改動帶另一任務，越積越大。

options.en: The work spread from the text into the recording and timing.
options.zh: 工作由文字擴到錄音及時間。

options.en: It was a linked sequence of follow-up changes rather than one isolated correction.
options.zh: 那是相連後續改動，而非孤立更正。

reply.explanationZh: 四句說累積路徑，不只以工作大稱雪球。

scene.promptZh: 小組有一人分享有用模板，其他人加例子再傳，幾天後已有更多班採用；你想描述正面擴散。哪句準確？

options.en: Interest snowballed as people added examples and shared the template.
options.zh: 大家加例再傳模板，興趣如雪球擴大。

options.en: The template remained with the first person and was not shared.
options.zh: 模板一直留首人，沒分享。

options.en: Interest grew before the template was shared and then stayed unchanged as examples were added.
options.zh: 模板分享前興趣已增加，之後加例時反而沒變。

scene.explanationZh: 題目把加例分享連到更多班採用，是正面累積；不是一直沒分享，也不是增長都在分享前。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 snowballed？

options.en: One delay leads to several connected delays.
options.zh: 一項延誤引出幾項相連延誤。

options.en: A small change remains isolated, with no added effect over time.
options.zh: 小改動一直孤立，隨時間沒增加影響。

options.en: Interest grows as each participant brings more people in.
options.zh: 每位參加者帶更多人，興趣擴大。

contrast.explanationZh: 沒有累積或擴大，不合雪球意象。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說「可能越積越大，所以現在已無法處理」，但你們剛發現仍可先定字幕再重錄。哪句較準確？

options.en: The linked tasks need planning, but the risk of growth does not mean action is already impossible.
options.zh: 相連任務需安排，但擴大風險不等於已不能行動。

options.en: We should rerecord the lines first and decide the captions afterwards.
options.zh: 應先重錄對白，再決定字幕。

options.en: The update was only an isolated spelling correction, with no linked recording or timing tasks.
options.zh: 更新只是一處獨立拼字修正，沒有相連錄音或時間工作。

dialogue.explanationZh: 已有相連字幕、重錄及核時任務，仍可先定字幕再錄；不能倒轉關鍵次序或縮成孤立拼字修正。

speaking.en: The small delay snowballed into extra work, so we listed the linked tasks before changing anything else.
speaking.zh: 小延誤連鎖帶額外工作，所以再改前先列相連任務。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把累積與處理連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你原只在大樓大堂放一箱自己不再讀的書供交換，鄰居陸續再捐多箱，現在大家想辦交換日。你要向管理員說明這正面擴大，並請一起安排暫存及分類空間，不先把所有箱子堵走廊。用一至兩句英文提出請求。

examples.en: One box of books has snowballed into enough donations for a swap day. Could we agree on temporary storage and sorting space before more boxes arrive?
examples.zh: 一箱書越積越大，捐書已足辦交換日；更多箱到前，可否議暫存及分類空間？

examples.en: The exchange idea snowballed as neighbours brought more books, so we now need somewhere to sort them. I would like to discuss a storage arrangement rather than leave the boxes in the corridor.
examples.zh: 鄰居帶更多書，交換構思越積越大，現需地方分類；我想談存放安排，不把箱留走廊。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以一箱到多箱及交換日說正面增長，向管理員提出暫存分類請求，不把新增需求當空間已批准或走廊可任用。

takeaways.en: The request snowballed into a wider discussion as more people added related questions.
takeaways.zh: 更多人補相關問題時，請求發展成較廣討論。

takeaways.en: A small error can snowball when later work depends on it.
takeaways.zh: 後續工作依賴小錯時，影響可能如雪球擴大。

brief.meaningEn: Make the decisive choice after relevant input or discussion.
brief.meaningZh: 在相關意見或討論後，作出最後決定。
brief.grammar: someone makes the final call on + issue; made in past; identify who has that decision role.
brief.register: Common informal decision expression. It is not the last telephone call in this use.
brief.boundaryZh: 最後決策角色不表示所有工作都由他做、不可聽人意見或選擇必定正確；需分清建議與決定。
brief.misconceptionZh: 有多個意見仍可有清楚最後決策者；未作決定前不要報成已定。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明誰決定哪項事情，保留協作及實際狀態。

sources.sentence: The editor will make the final call on the design.

listening.en: The group will compare the cover drafts, but the editor will make the final call on which version goes to print after checking the title and credits.
listening.zh: 小組會比較封面草稿，但編輯核對標題署名後，才最後決定哪版印刷。

options.en: The editor chooses the printed cover after the checks and comparison.
options.zh: 比較及核對後，編輯選印刷封面。

options.en: The group has already sent a cover to print before the editor checks it.
options.zh: 編輯核前，小組已送封面印刷。

options.en: The printer chooses the title and credits without editorial input.
options.zh: 印刷者沒有編輯意見就選標題署名。

options.en: The editor’s final call is a telephone confirmation to the printer rather than a choice between covers.
options.zh: 編輯的最後一通是向印刷者電話確認，而非選封面。

listening.explanationZh: 本句final call指由編輯選哪版印，非最後一通電話；比較及標題署名核對都在最後選擇之前。

reply.promptZh: 封面比較及核對後，誰會決定送印版本？
reply.promptEn: Who will decide which cover goes to print after the comparison and checks?

options.en: The editor will choose which draft goes to print.
options.zh: 編輯會選哪草稿送印。

options.en: The editor will make the final call on the cover.
options.zh: 編輯會對封面作最後決定。

options.en: The final choice belongs to the editor after the group’s comparison.
options.zh: 小組比較後，最後選擇由編輯負責。

options.en: The group can give input, while the editor settles the printed version.
options.zh: 小組可給意見，由編輯定印刷版。

reply.explanationZh: 四句說最後決策分工，不抹比較及核對。

scene.promptZh: 設計比賽小組可提出方案，但已議定由組長聽完各人理由後選提交版，目前未選。哪句準確？

options.en: The leader will make the final call after hearing the team’s reasons.
options.zh: 組長聽團隊理由後會作最後決定。

options.en: The submission has already been selected before the discussion.
options.zh: 討論前，提交版已選。

options.en: The whole team has already selected the version without waiting for the leader’s decision.
options.zh: 全組已不用等組長決定，選定提交版。

scene.explanationZh: 已議定組長聽理由後作最後決定，目前未選，不是全組或討論前已定。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 she makes the final call 得出？

options.en: She is responsible for the decisive choice in context.
options.zh: 情境中，她負責最後選擇。

options.en: She cannot consider anyone else’s advice.
options.zh: 她不能考慮任何別人意見。

options.en: Others may contribute before her decision.
options.zh: 她決定前，其他人可有貢獻。

contrast.explanationZh: 最後決策者仍可聽意見。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴問「編輯最後決定，所以我們比較草稿沒用了？」但比較會給她依據。哪句較準確？

options.en: Our comparison can inform her choice even though she is responsible for settling it.
options.zh: 我們比較可給她決定依據，儘管最後由她定。

options.en: We should postpone comparing the drafts until after the editor has made her choice.
options.zh: 應等編輯選定後，才比較草稿。

options.en: We should send a draft to print now and leave the title and credit checks until later.
options.zh: 現在先送一份草稿印刷，標題署名稍後核。

dialogue.explanationZh: 比較可給編輯決定依據，核對也應在送印前；不延至選後才比，或核前先印。

speaking.en: She will make the final call after considering the team’s reasons, not before hearing them.
speaking.zh: 她會考慮團隊理由後才作最後決定，不是聽前。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把決策角色及協作連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們替祖母挑幾段口述故事公開在家庭網頁，家人可提建議，但已約定祖母聽過剪輯版本後自己最後決定公開哪些，尚未獲准。你想向家人說明程序，不把幫剪輯當已得許可。用一至兩句英文表達。
writing.selfCheckZh: 清楚交代祖母聽版後才最後決定、家人提供建議，保留未獲許可，不把剪輯工作當批准。

examples.en: Grandma will make the final call on which stories we share after hearing the edited versions. Our suggestions can help, but we should not publish before she decides.
examples.zh: 祖母聽剪輯版後，會最後決定公開哪些故事。我們建議可幫忙，但她決定前不應刊登。

examples.en: We can prepare the clips and explain our choices, while Grandma makes the final call about publication. Editing the files is not the same as receiving her permission.
examples.zh: 我們可準備片段並解釋選擇，公開與否仍由祖母最後決定。剪檔不等於獲她許可。

takeaways.en: The coordinator made the final call after comparing the proposed routes.
takeaways.zh: 協調員比較建議路線後，作最後決定。

takeaways.en: We need to know who will make the final call before presenting several competing drafts.
takeaways.zh: 提出幾個競爭草稿前，我們需知誰作最後決定。

brief.meaningEn: The possible gains, losses or consequences of a decision are serious or important.
brief.meaningZh: 某決定可能帶來的得失或後果重大。
brief.grammar: the stakes are high when + situation; were for past; explain the actual consequences at issue.
brief.register: Established gambling metaphor used well beyond money or betting.
brief.boundaryZh: 後果重大不表示答案已明、失敗必定發生或不能行動；需具體後果，不只把事情稱重要。
brief.misconceptionZh: 宜按情境重要性說明，不把任何小喜好都誇成重大得失，也不由壓力推唯一方案。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出決定涉及甚麼重要後果，並以核對及評估回應。
